ops.body:
**OAuth `tag:vault` widen — console side DONE (acct-14, agent-browser-with-cookies).** The old fleet node-key minter `kEf5UEAw3711CNTRL` had scope `auth_keys` + tags `tag:hermes/metal/bluebubbles` (no vault); OAuth client tags are immutable, so recreated.

**New client `kxHMfk1JTB21CNTRL`** created + verified: scope `auth_keys` (Read+Write), tags `tag:hermes`, `tag:metal`, `tag:bluebubbles`, **`tag:vault`**. Secret captured to `~/.yclaw/oauth-new-client.txt` (mode 600; never printed to any transcript). Old client `kEf5UEAw3711CNTRL` LEFT ACTIVE deliberately — don't delete until the keychain swap is verified (deleting it before the swap would break all node-key minting).

**Remaining (USER, Terminal.app — I can't write the keychain from a background session):**
1. Store the new creds into the yclaw keychain (`~/Library/Keychains/yclaw.keychain-db`, account `$(id -un)`), services `yclaw-ts-oauth-client-id` / `yclaw-ts-oauth-client-secret`, values from the 600 file. Via `yclaw secret set` once reconcile lands, or raw `security add-generic-password -U`.
2. Verify (`yclaw secret reconcile vault --dry-run`, or a tag:vault key mint succeeds).
3. Then delete the old client `kEf5UEAw3711CNTRL` (I can do this via the console on request) and `rm ~/.yclaw/oauth-new-client.txt`.

This clears one of the two P3 blockers; the other is the reconcile session landing + `reconcile vault` minting vault's bundle.
